overview: This Senate resolution recognizes May as Jewish American Heritage Month, a time to celebrate the contributions of Jewish Americans, and calls on leaders to counter antisemitism (hostility or prejudice against Jewish people). It reviews more than 350 years of Jewish American history, including military service and several Medal of Honor recipients, and cites recent deadly attacks and reports showing antisemitic incidents in the United States at very high levels since October 2023. The resolution calls on elected officials, faith leaders, and community leaders to condemn antisemitism and educate the public about Jewish American contributions, and commits the Senate to protecting the safety of Jewish Americans and the religious freedom of all Americans. It does not change any law or spending. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on May 19, 2026.
for: Supporters say the resolution honors Jewish Americans' long contributions to the country and sends a clear message against rising antisemitic threats and violence.
against: Critics say the resolution is largely symbolic: it calls for action against antisemitism but does not itself fund security, change any law, or create new protections.
